sessions.title: Foundation Skills FS01 - Week 1 Lesson Plan
sessions.topic: Workshop Safety, Hazards, Housekeeping and Occupational Expectations
sessions.sowReference: Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills SOW v1.2 | FS01 | Week 1
sessions.programme: Shared Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills | all mapped routes
sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This shared occupational session develops safe work-area preparation, hazard controls, equipment responsibility, communication and professional workshop behaviours. Pathway examples are used for Light Vehicle, Heavy Vehicle, Paint, Panel and Autocare apprentices.
aims: Develop safe and professional working expectations for the training centre and workplace.
Recognise common workshop hazards and select suitable controls.
Understand responsibilities for housekeeping, tools, communication and escalation.
learningObjectives: Identify at least five hazards and state an appropriate control for each.
Explain common safety signs, emergency points and reporting routes.
Complete a concise safe-work-area or hazard record using clear terminology.
Contribute effectively to a team safety task and identify one workplace action.

theory.activity: Introduce shared workshop safety expectations: signs, emergency arrangements, safe routes, reporting, housekeeping and individual responsibility. Use current pathway examples including vehicle-lifting and wheel-handling areas, preparation/mixing/spray areas, welding/pulling zones and fast-fit work areas.
theory.checks: Baseline questions; safety-sign sort; correct misconceptions. Stretch: justify controls using the hierarchy of control.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 1 materials; safety signs; workshop map; pathway photographs; PPE/RPE examples.

practical.activity: Guided site and workshop safety walk. Apprentices identify hazards, emergency points, restricted areas, equipment-storage expectations and safe routes. Discuss how hazards differ across Light, Heavy, Paint, Panel and Autocare work areas.
practical.checks: Use targeted questioning at each stop. Support with a visual checklist; extend by asking apprentices to rank risks and explain escalation.
practical.resources: Site hazard checklist; workshop map; safety-sign guide; clipboard/tablet; PPE.

application.activity: Team hazard-identification and safe-work-area task. Apprentices inspect an allocated area or scenario, identify hazards, select controls, assign responsibilities and present findings. Reinforce respectful communication and leaving the area safe and tidy.
application.checks: Observe safe behaviour, communication and contribution. Challenge secure learners to explain consequences of weak controls.
application.resources: Hazard scenario cards; risk-control worksheet; workshop area or photographs; housekeeping checklist.

consolidation.activity: Consolidation and learning impact. Apprentices complete a concise safe-work-area/hazard record, correct it following feedback and state one action they will apply in the workplace.
consolidation.checks: Review accuracy and terminology. Exit question: identify one hazard, one control and the correct reporting route. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
consolidation.resources: Hazard record; learner reflection; tutor observation notes; workplace action slip.

nonEligible.activity: 0-10 wellbeing check, introductions and confirmation of employer and apprenticeship pathway. Use remaining time for immediate pastoral needs and essential programme administration.
nonEligible.checks: Pastoral and administrative opening only. Record separately from OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: wellbeing-check record; cohort list; support information.

nonEligible.activity: Foundation Skills programme overview, contact-sheet completion, ground rules, break arrangements, phone expectations, OTJ-record explanation, online-system access and other onboarding or programme administration.
nonEligible.checks: Do not include this period in eligible OTJ. Check required forms and access arrangements are complete.
nonEligible.resources: Contact sheet; code of conduct; OTJ log guidance; online access details; programme information.

workplaceFollowUp.activity:
Workplace follow-up
• Identify one real workplace hazard or housekeeping issue with the employer/mentor.
• Record the control used and how it protects people, vehicles, equipment or the environment.
workplaceFollowUp.checks:
Trainer preparation
• Check workshop access, emergency information, safety signs and allocated task areas.
• Prepare pathway examples for Light, Heavy, Paint, Panel and Autocare where represented.
• Confirm support needs and keep all non-eligible periods separate from OTJ.

other.activity: Post-lesson impact: What can apprentices now identify, explain or complete that they could not do at the start? | Follow-up: Who needs additional support or stretch, what is the next action and when will it be reviewed?

howLearningChecked: Start: Baseline questions and a short safety-sign or hazard-identification task.

sessions.title: Foundation Skills FS02 - Week 2 Lesson Plan
sessions.topic: Health and Safety, Tools, Equipment and Safe Vehicle Support
sessions.sowReference: Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills SOW v1.2 | FS02 | Week 2
sessions.programme: Shared Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills | all mapped routes
sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops safe selection, inspection and use of tools and equipment, including safe lifting and supporting. Examples include light-vehicle jacks and torque tools, heavy-vehicle lifts, approved vehicle-lifting systems and high-capacity equipment, paint preparation equipment, panel repair systems and autocare fast-fit tools.
aims: Reinforce health and safety responsibilities and safe workshop conduct.
Develop safe pre-use inspection and selection of tools and equipment.
Introduce safe lifting, supporting, SWL and torque-control principles.
learningObjectives: Explain SWL and why equipment condition and calibration matter.
Complete a dynamic risk assessment for a lifting or support task.
Select and use appropriate tools safely under supervision.
Record equipment checks and identify when equipment must be removed from use.

theory.activity: Recap workshop safety and introduce safe working loads, lifting/supporting, tool condition, calibration and correct selection. Compare pathway tools: LV jacks/stands and torque wrenches; HV lifts, approved vehicle-lifting systems, wheel handlers and high-capacity equipment; Paint DA sanders, spray guns and panel stands; Panel welders, riveters and pulling systems; Autocare tyre and brake equipment.
theory.checks: Question prior experience and challenge unsafe assumptions. Use tool photographs or real examples.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 2 materials; tool samples; SWL labels; calibration examples; pathway tool cards.

practical.activity: Demonstrate safe vehicle lifting/supporting and torque-tool use, including pre-use checks, correct positions, exclusion zones, communication and safe lowering. Apprentices complete a guided checklist.
practical.checks: Observe sequence and stop unsafe actions. Support with a step card; stretch by comparing equipment limits across pathways.
practical.resources: Vehicle or rig; jack/stands or suitable lifting equipment; torque wrench; technical data; PPE.

application.activity: Supervised practical task: prepare the area, complete a dynamic risk assessment, lift/support or simulate the task, use selected tools correctly and restore the area.
application.checks: Observation against safe-working criteria; targeted questions on SWL, damage prevention and reporting. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
application.resources: Dynamic risk assessment; lifting/support checklist; tool inspection sheet.

consolidation.activity: Quality review and technical record. Apprentices identify defects in tool/equipment scenarios, explain actions and complete a concise inspection record.
consolidation.checks: Check accuracy and escalation decisions. Give feedback followed by correction. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
consolidation.resources: Tool defect cards; inspection record; calibration/maintenance examples.

nonEligible.activity: 0-10 wellbeing check, previous OTJ record review and immediate support. Complete only essential administration or standalone Functional Skills according to individual need.
nonEligible.checks: Record separately from eligible OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: wellbeing-check record; OTJ record; support/FS materials.

nonEligible.activity: ERR, contact-sheet or online-course tracking and any routine programme administration.
nonEligible.checks: Exclude from OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: ERR/online tracker; programme records.

workplaceFollowUp.activity:
Workplace follow-up
• Identify one lifting, supporting or tool-control procedure used at work.
• Record the equipment check, SWL or torque information used.
workplaceFollowUp.checks:
Trainer preparation
• Confirm suitable equipment and technical data are available and serviceable.
• Prepare pathway-specific tool examples without creating separate classes.
• Check learner PPE and planned support.

sessions.title: Foundation Skills FS03 - Week 3 Lesson Plan
sessions.topic: Hybrid and High-Voltage Vehicle Awareness
sessions.sowReference: Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills SOW v1.2 | FS03 | Week 3
sessions.programme: Shared Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills | all mapped routes
sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops recognition of electrified-vehicle hazards, safe approach, competence boundaries and escalation. The depth of work differs by pathway, but every apprentice must recognise high-voltage vehicles and avoid unsafe preparation, repair, inspection or refinishing activity.
aims: Introduce hybrid and electric vehicle identification and warning systems.
Develop safe approach, key-control and exclusion principles.
Clarify limits of competence and correct escalation routes.
learningObjectives: Identify common hybrid/EV labels, components and high-voltage colours.
Explain at least four significant hazards and suitable controls.
Complete a safe-approach checklist for a vehicle or scenario.
State when work must stop and an authorised person must be involved.

theory.activity: Introduce hybrid/EV types, identification, warning labels, orange cables, energy storage, automatic movement/start risks and the role of authorised persons. Use examples from light, heavy, body repair and autocare workplaces.
theory.checks: Use image questioning and correct misconceptions about keys, charging and isolation.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 3 materials; EV/hybrid presentation; component images; warning labels.

practical.activity: Guided vehicle-identification and safe-approach activity. Apprentices locate identifiers, establish vehicle status, control keys, select signage/exclusion and identify information required before work.
practical.checks: Observe safe sequence. Support with checklist; stretch through complex scenarios or heavy-vehicle/bodyshop examples.
practical.resources: Vehicle/rig or scenario images; safe-approach checklist; barriers/signage; PPE.

application.activity: Practical hazard scenarios: decide whether routine inspection, lifting, paint preparation, panel work, battery checks or electrical tasks can proceed. Record stop, isolate, refer and communicate decisions.
application.checks: Question rationale and require evidence-based decisions. Correct unsafe boundaries. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
application.resources: Pathway scenario cards; technical information; decision record.

consolidation.activity: Consolidation, questioning and corrected safe-work plan. Apprentices explain one workplace application for their pathway.
consolidation.checks: Compare start/end responses and set an action where needed. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
consolidation.resources: Safe-work plan; questioning record; learner reflection.

nonEligible.activity: MME, previous OTJ log support, brain warmer and essential programme activity.
nonEligible.checks: Record separately from OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: wellbeing and OTJ records; starter materials.

nonEligible.activity: ERR, online-course completion or formal knowledge-test administration.
nonEligible.checks: Formal testing and administration are excluded from OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: ERR/online course/test records.

workplaceFollowUp.activity:
Workplace follow-up
• Identify how electrified vehicles are recognised and controlled at the workplace.
• Confirm the person or procedure used for isolation and escalation.
workplaceFollowUp.checks:
Trainer preparation
• Check the training vehicle/rig and ensure no live work beyond learner competence.
• Prepare pathway-specific scenarios for the cohort.
• Confirm barriers, signage and emergency arrangements.

sessions.title: Foundation Skills FS04 - Week 4 Lesson Plan
sessions.topic: Fire Safety, Battery Awareness and Basic Electrical Safety
sessions.sowReference: Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills SOW v1.2 | FS04 | Week 4
sessions.programme: Shared Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills | all mapped routes
sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops fire prevention, battery safety and basic electrical risk awareness. Applications include fuel and solvent risks, 12/24-volt systems, charging, welding equipment, spray-booth controls, workshop electrical tools and safe use of a multimeter within defined limits.
aims: Recognise fire classes, common causes and suitable controls.
Understand lead-acid, lithium and low-voltage battery hazards.
Develop safe basic multimeter use and electrical-risk reporting.
learningObjectives: Explain the fire triangle and identify suitable extinguisher types.
Identify battery and charging hazards and required PPE/ventilation.
Use a multimeter safely for a simple voltage or resistance measurement.
State when electrical work must stop and be escalated.

theory.activity: Teach fire triangle, fire classes, extinguisher identification, alarms, evacuation and common vehicle-workshop causes: fuels, solvents, hot work, static, charging, electrical faults and overheating.
theory.checks: Question selection and emphasise evacuation/raising alarm before firefighting.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 4 materials; extinguishers/signage; fire triangle; pathway scenarios.

practical.activity: Battery awareness: lead-acid and lithium hazards, hydrogen, acid, thermal risk, charging, handling, isolation, ventilation and PPE. Compare 12V light/autocare systems, 24V heavy systems and bodyshop risks before welding or refinishing.
practical.checks: Use scenario questions and identify unsafe arrangements.
practical.resources: Battery samples/images; chargers; PPE; SDS/technical information; safety checklist.

application.activity: Demonstrate multimeter inspection, lead connection, range/function selection and safe simple voltage/resistance measurement. Apprentices practise within low-voltage limits.
application.checks: Observe correct connections and stop unsafe use. Support with step card. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
application.resources: Multimeters; low-voltage battery/variable resistor or training board; test leads; PPE.

consolidation.activity: Review readings and complete fire/battery/electrical control scenarios. Learners correct errors and state reporting routes.
consolidation.checks: Check understanding through targeted questions and corrected records. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
consolidation.resources: Fire/battery worksheet; measurement record; escalation card.

nonEligible.activity: MME, OTJ log support, brain warmer and essential programme administration.
nonEligible.checks: Record separately from OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: wellbeing and OTJ records; starter.

nonEligible.activity: Online-course/ERR tracking or formal assessment activity.
nonEligible.checks: Exclude formal testing and administration from OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: Online/ERR/test records.

Workplace follow-up
• Locate fire and battery controls at work and discuss them with a supervisor.
• Record one pathway-specific fire or electrical risk and the control used.
workplaceFollowUp.checks:
Trainer preparation
• Check extinguishers/signage examples and low-voltage training equipment.
• Ensure multimeters and leads are serviceable.
• Prepare pathway scenarios and PPE examples.

sessions.sowReference: Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills SOW v1.2 | FS05 | Week 5

sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops accurate measurement, units, calibration awareness, technical-data use and tolerance. Applications include brake discs and tread depth, heavy-vehicle hubs and pressures, paint ratios/viscosity/temperature, panel alignment/gaps and autocare inspection data.
aims: Develop accurate use of common measuring tools and units.
Understand datum points, tolerances, calibration and quality requirements.
Apply technical information and record results clearly.
learningObjectives: Select and use at least three measuring tools correctly.
Convert or interpret relevant metric/imperial values.
Compare measurements with a specification or tolerance.
Complete a clear measured-results record and identify corrective action.

theory.activity: Teach metric/imperial units, accuracy, precision, datum, tolerance, calibration and equipment selection. Introduce vernier, micrometer, engineer rule, DTI, pressure/tread gauges and torque tools.
theory.checks: Use prior-knowledge questions and tool identification.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 5 materials; measuring tools; technical data; pathway examples.

practical.activity: Demonstrate correct reading, zero/calibration checks and care of equipment. Pathway examples: LV brake disc/run-out; HV hub/drum/air pressure; Paint ratios, viscosity and temperature; Panel dimensions/gaps; Autocare tread/pressure/geometry.
practical.checks: Check hand position, zeroing and reading. Provide scales or visual prompts where needed.
practical.resources: Components/materials; vernier; micrometer; DTI; rules; gauges; torque wrench; data sheets.

application.activity: Practical measurement task. Apprentices select at least three suitable measurements, record units, compare to specification and identify serviceability or quality implications.
application.checks: Observe safe tool use and verify readings. Challenge secure learners with conversion or tolerance decisions. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
application.resources: Measurement task sheet; components/panels/materials; calculators; technical data.

consolidation.activity: Quality review, calculations and corrective practice. Apprentices improve weak measurements and complete a technical record using correct terminology.
consolidation.checks: Compare first and final readings; feedback followed by re-measurement. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
consolidation.resources: Measured-results record; calculation sheet; observation notes.

sessions.sowReference: Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills SOW v1.2 | FS06 | Week 6

sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops recognition of fasteners, following drawings, safe hand/tool use, marking out, measurement, tolerance, teamwork and housekeeping. Pathway examples include service fasteners, heavy-duty fixings, trim and panel fasteners, rivets/bonding preparations and wheel/security components.
aims: Recognise common fasteners, washers and their purposes.
Follow a simple engineering drawing and risk-controlled process.
Develop safe fabrication, measurement and quality-checking habits.
learningObjectives: Select a suitable fastener or fixing for a stated purpose.
Interpret dimensions, datum and tolerance from a drawing.
Complete a supervised fabrication/equivalent task safely and accurately.
Record quality findings and improvements.

theory.activity: Teach fastener types, threads, washers, locking methods, advantages/limitations and safe tool selection. Use pathway examples from vehicle service, heavy vehicles, paint trim removal, panel joining and autocare wheel/component work.
theory.checks: Tool/fastener questioning and matching task.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 6 materials; fastener samples; pathway examples; tool-selection cards.

practical.activity: Brief the engineering drawing and fabrication/equivalent task. Complete dynamic risk assessment, identify datum, dimensions, tolerances, sequence, tools and quality criteria. Demonstrate marking out, drilling and chamfering as applicable.
practical.checks: Check interpretation before work starts. Support with enlarged drawing; stretch through tighter tolerances or justification. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
practical.resources: Drawing; steel block/material; marking and drilling tools; measuring tools; PPE.

application.activity: Supervised practical task with safe tool use, teamwork, measurement and housekeeping. Apprentices pause for quality checks and corrections.
application.checks: Observe safe technique and measurement. Feedback is developmental, not formal sign-off. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
application.resources: Fabrication/equivalent task; tool and measurement equipment; QA sheet.

nonEligible.activity: MME, OTJ log support and essential programme administration. Confirm first-aid rotation arrangements.
nonEligible.checks: Record separately from OTJ.

Examples include 12V light/autocare systems, 24V heavy systems, bodyshop electrical safety and paint-booth/equipment controls.
aims: Develop safe basic multimeter function and calibration checks.
Record and interpret simple voltage and resistance readings.
Reinforce accurate practical work, tolerance, teamwork and quality.
learningObjectives: Inspect and prepare a multimeter safely.
Obtain and record simple voltage and resistance readings.
Explain the limits of basic testing and when to escalate.
Complete or quality-check the fabrication/equivalent task against tolerance.

theory.activity: Teach multimeter purpose, inspection, leads, functions, range, polarity, calibration/zero checks and safe limitations. Compare pathway uses and emphasise that high-voltage testing is outside this basic session.
theory.checks: Question safe sequence and identify damaged-equipment actions.
theory.resources: Foundation Session 7 materials; multimeters; visual guide; pathway scenarios.

practical.activity: Guided basic electrical measurement using low-voltage battery and resistance components. Apprentices record results and explain whether readings are plausible.
practical.checks: Observe connections and function selection. Correct errors before energising. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
practical.resources: Low-voltage battery/variable resistor/training board; multimeters; result sheet; PPE.

application.activity: Fabrication continuation or equivalent quality task: measure to tolerance, identify defects, correct where possible, complete housekeeping and technical write-up.
application.checks: Observe safe tools, accuracy and teamwork. Challenge with root-cause questions. Stretch: compare two approaches, justify the more effective and state one workplace consequence.
application.resources: Fabrication tools/materials; drawing; measuring equipment; QA record.

sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops accurate, professional practice for customer service scenarios. Clear decisions and records support customer confidence, efficient workshop operation, business protection, traceability and appropriate escalation.
aims: Develop secure occupational knowledge and terminology for customer service scenarios.
Apply safe, accurate and methodical working procedures through the planned task or scenario.
Produce, review and improve evidence that demonstrates decisions, quality and workplace application.
learningObjectives: Identify and explain at least three key principles, risks or controls relevant to customer service scenarios.
Select and use relevant technical information, workplace procedures, tools, equipment or documentation for the planned task.
Complete a task or scenario linked to customer service scenarios safely, accurately and in the correct sequence.
Record findings clearly and justify at least one decision using technical information or workplace procedure.

theory.activity: Tutor-led session exploring different customer service scenarios including complaints, misunderstandings and service delays. Explanation of customer expectations, workshop limitations and how poor communication can escalate issues.
theory.checks: Baseline/retrieval check; correct misconceptions. Support: vocabulary bank or annotated visual. Stretch: apply the principles to a less familiar risk or quality issue.
theory.resources: Complaint forms; policy documents

practical.activity: Structured role-play activities where learners handle realistic customer complaints, including incorrect work, delays and cost disputes. Tutor models effective responses before learners practise independently. Observation used to assess communication skills, tone, and ability to remain professional.
practical.checks: Observe sequence, safety and use of tools/information; give immediate corrective feedback. Support: tutor model and sequenced task checklist. Stretch: compare methods and justify the safer or more accurate approach.
practical.resources: Complaint forms; policy documents

application.activity: Application linking complaint scenarios to documentation and evidence. Learners complete written records of customer interactions including notes on issues raised and actions taken. Emphasis on accuracy, clarity and accountability.
application.checks: Review the developing output and reasoning. Support: model record, worked example or extra checkpoint. Stretch: evaluate efficiency, quality and customer/business impact.
application.resources: Complaint forms; policy documents

consolidation.activity: Consolidation through group discussion reviewing responses and identifying best practice. Tutor-led questioning checks understanding of complaint handling procedures. Evidence generated through written documentation, observation and questioning.
consolidation.checks: End check: review evidence, require correction and record impact. Support: targeted recap or repeat demonstration. Stretch: justify the decision and explain workplace transfer.
consolidation.resources: Evidence: Complaint records; response drafts

nonEligible.activity: Mood, Motivation and Energy (0-10) check and individual programme activity. Record separately from eligible OTJ.
nonEligible.checks: Pastoral/administrative opening only. Record separately and do not count as eligible OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: Mood, Motivation and Energy record or programme record.

workplaceFollowUp.activity:
Workplace follow-up
• With the employer/mentor, identify or apply one workplace example linked to customer service scenarios.
• Retain a suitable record and explain its effect on safety, quality, efficiency or the customer.
workplaceFollowUp.checks:
Trainer preparation
• Check the work area, current technical information, tools/equipment and relevant PPE/RPE.
• Prepare session materials and evidence records: Mood, Motivation and Energy record or programme record.; Complaint forms; policy documents.
• Confirm support needs, reasonable adjustments, any approved recognition-of-prior-learning change and the evidence location. Keep formal assessment, gateway decisions and administration separate from eligible learning.

sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops the knowledge and practical judgement needed for advanced brake diagnostics. Following technical information and safe procedures supports vehicle safety, work quality, efficient diagnosis or repair, customer confidence and clear accountability.
aims: Develop secure occupational knowledge and terminology for advanced brake diagnostics.
Apply safe, accurate and methodical working procedures through the planned task or scenario.
Produce, review and improve evidence that demonstrates decisions, quality and workplace application.
learningObjectives: Identify and explain at least three key principles, risks or controls relevant to advanced brake diagnostics.
Select and use relevant technical information, workplace procedures, tools, equipment or documentation for the planned task.
Complete a task or scenario linked to advanced brake diagnostics safely, accurately and in the correct sequence.
Record findings clearly and justify at least one decision using technical information or workplace procedure.

theory.activity: Detailed theory session covering advanced brake system operation including ABS components such as wheel speed sensors, tone rings, hydraulic control unit and ECU interaction.
theory.checks: Baseline/retrieval check; correct misconceptions. Support: vocabulary bank or annotated visual. Stretch: apply the principles to a less familiar risk or quality issue.
theory.resources: ABS rigs; scan tools; PPE

practical.activity: Structured practical session identifying ABS components on training vehicles. Learners locate sensors, inspect wiring routes and identify mounting positions. Tutor demonstrates visual inspection techniques and highlights common issues such as damaged wiring, corrosion and incorrect sensor gaps.
practical.checks: Observe sequence, safety and use of tools/information; give immediate corrective feedback. Support: tutor model and sequenced task checklist. Stretch: compare methods and justify the safer or more accurate approach.
practical.resources: ABS rigs; scan tools; PPE

application.activity: Application activity diagnosing brake and ABS-related faults based on given scenarios including ABS warning light, intermittent braking issues and vibration under braking. Learners interpret symptoms, suggest possible root causes and record findings on a structured diagnostic worksheet or job card.
application.checks: Review the developing output and reasoning. Support: model record, worked example or extra checkpoint. Stretch: evaluate efficiency, quality and customer/business impact.
application.resources: ABS rigs; scan tools; PPE

consolidation.activity: Consolidation through group discussion reviewing diagnostic decisions and common errors. Tutor-led questioning checks understanding of system operation and fault impact. Short knowledge check reinforces key learning points.
consolidation.checks: End check: review evidence, require correction and record impact. Support: targeted recap or repeat demonstration. Stretch: justify the decision and explain workplace transfer.
consolidation.resources: Evidence: Scan logs; repair sheet; test results

practical.resources: Alignment rig; balancer; PPE

application.activity: Application activity where learners diagnose alignment-related faults using scenarios such as vehicle pulling, uneven tyre wear and off-centre steering wheel. Learners link symptoms to potential causes including worn components, incorrect adjustments or accident damage.
application.checks: Review the developing output and reasoning. Support: model record, worked example or extra checkpoint. Stretch: evaluate efficiency, quality and customer/business impact.
application.resources: Alignment rig; balancer; PPE

consolidation.activity: Consolidation through questioning and group discussion reviewing diagnostic decisions. Tutor reinforces importance of accurate interpretation and linking faults to root causes. Evidence generated through written diagnostic tasks and questioning.

sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session develops accurate, professional practice for customer dispute resolution. Clear decisions and records support customer confidence, efficient workshop operation, business protection, traceability and appropriate escalation.
aims: Develop secure occupational knowledge and terminology for customer dispute resolution.
Apply safe, accurate and methodical working procedures through the planned task or scenario.
Produce, review and improve evidence that demonstrates decisions, quality and workplace application.
learningObjectives: Identify and explain at least three key principles, risks or controls relevant to customer dispute resolution.
Select and use relevant technical information, workplace procedures, tools, equipment or documentation for the planned task.
Complete a task or scenario linked to customer dispute resolution safely, accurately and in the correct sequence.
Record findings clearly and justify at least one decision using technical information or workplace procedure.

theory.activity: Theory session covering customer dispute resolution including complaint handling procedures, escalation routes and basic consumer rights awareness. Discussion of common causes of disputes such as incorrect work, delays or pricing issues.
theory.checks: Baseline/retrieval check; correct misconceptions. Support: vocabulary bank or annotated visual. Stretch: apply the principles to a less familiar risk or quality issue.
theory.resources: Templates; policy documents

practical.activity: Structured role-play activities where learners handle realistic dispute scenarios. Situations include disagreement over work carried out, dissatisfaction with service and cost challenges. Tutor models effective responses before learners practise independently.
practical.checks: Observe sequence, safety and use of tools/information; give immediate corrective feedback. Support: tutor model and sequenced task checklist. Stretch: compare methods and justify the safer or more accurate approach.
practical.resources: Templates; policy documents

application.activity: Application linking dispute scenarios to documentation and evidence. Learners complete written records of customer interactions including issue description, actions taken and outcomes. Tutor reinforces importance of accurate, clear and defensible documentation.
application.checks: Review the developing output and reasoning. Support: model record, worked example or extra checkpoint. Stretch: evaluate efficiency, quality and customer/business impact.
application.resources: Templates; policy documents

consolidation.activity: Consolidation through group discussion reviewing approaches taken and identifying best practice. Tutor-led questioning checks understanding of dispute handling and legal considerations. Evidence generated through written documentation, observation and questioning responses.
consolidation.checks: End check: review evidence, require correction and record impact. Support: targeted recap or repeat demonstration. Stretch: justify the decision and explain workplace transfer.
consolidation.resources: Evidence: Dispute log; response letter; reflection

nonEligible.activity: Mood, Motivation and Energy (0-10) check and individual programme activity. Record separately from eligible OTJ.
nonEligible.checks: Pastoral/administrative opening only. Record separately and do not count as eligible OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: Mood, Motivation and Energy record or programme record.

• Complete the required block review, recording learning, confidence, independence, evidence and next steps.

workplaceFollowUp.checks:

• Confirm support needs, reasonable adjustments, any approved recognition-of-prior-learning change and the evidence location. Keep formal assessment, gateway decisions and administration separate from eligible learning.

theory.activity: Detailed theory session introducing 5S principles including sort, set in order, shine, standardise and sustain. Tutor explains how organisation impacts safety, efficiency and productivity. Discussion of common workshop hazards such as oil spills, poor storage and clutter, linking these to accident risk.
theory.checks: Baseline/retrieval check; correct misconceptions. Support: vocabulary bank or annotated visual. Stretch: apply the principles to a less familiar risk or quality issue.

application.checks: Review the developing output and reasoning. Support: model record, worked example or extra checkpoint. Stretch: evaluate efficiency, quality and customer/business impact.
application.resources: Housekeeping checklists; COSHH information; storage labels; PPE

consolidation.resources: Evidence: Housekeeping checks; safety records; workstation photos; reflection

theory.activity: Detailed theory session covering emergency response, near-miss reporting and environmental safety in the automotive workshop.

application.resources: Risk assessment templates; PPE; environmental guidance; emergency procedures

consolidation.activity: Consolidation through group review of scenario responses and incident documentation. The tutor challenges learners on whether their actions protected people, vehicles, property and the environment. sessions.focusLine: Mapped occupational duties | K1-K34; S1-S8, S10-S26; B1-B5 | Scheduled at block end
sessions.blockPeriod: Final Consolidation, Corrective Learning and EPA Readiness Training | Months 24-29
sessions.sowReference: Autocare Technician Level 2 SOW v4.1 | Block 10 | Week 112
sessions.occupationalRelevance: Occupational relevance: This session integrates prior learning through targeted ksb gap learning and corrective practical. Methodical practice, accurate evidence and corrective feedback strengthen safe independent performance, professional judgement and readiness for the next stage of the apprenticeship.
aims: Develop secure occupational knowledge and terminology for targeted ksb gap learning and corrective practical.
Apply safe, accurate and methodical working procedures through the planned task or scenario.
Produce, review and improve evidence that demonstrates decisions, quality and workplace application.
learningObjectives: Identify and explain at least three key principles, risks or controls relevant to targeted ksb gap learning and corrective practical.
Select and use relevant technical information, workplace procedures, tools, equipment or documentation for the planned task.
Complete a task or scenario linked to targeted ksb gap learning and corrective practical safely, accurately and in the correct sequence.
Record findings clearly and justify at least one decision using technical information or workplace procedure.

theory.activity: Review the individual KSB gap analysis and agree the targeted learning plan.
theory.checks: Baseline/retrieval check; correct misconceptions. Support: vocabulary bank or annotated visual. Stretch: apply the principles to a less familiar risk or quality issue.
theory.resources: Individual gap plan; relevant tools/vehicles; technical data; evidence checklist.

practical.activity: Complete targeted practical development.
practical.checks: Observe sequence, safety and use of tools/information; give immediate corrective feedback. Support: tutor model and sequenced task checklist. Stretch: compare methods and justify the safer or more accurate approach.
practical.resources: Individual gap plan; relevant tools/vehicles; technical data; evidence checklist.

application.activity: Repeat or extend the task with reduced support and improved documentation.
application.checks: Review the developing output and reasoning. Support: model record, worked example or extra checkpoint. Stretch: evaluate efficiency, quality and customer/business impact.
application.resources: Individual gap plan; relevant tools/vehicles; technical data; evidence checklist.

consolidation.activity: Feedback, reflection and evidence quality check.
consolidation.checks: End check: review evidence, require correction and record impact. Support: targeted recap or repeat demonstration. Stretch: justify the decision and explain workplace transfer.
consolidation.resources: Evidence: Updated gap plan; practical evidence; feedback record; corrected documentation.

nonEligible.activity: Non-eligible: Mood, Motivation and Energy (0-10) check and programme administration.
nonEligible.checks: Pastoral/administrative opening only. Record separately and do not count as eligible OTJ.
nonEligible.resources: Mood, Motivation and Energy record or programme record.

workplaceFollowUp.activity:
Workplace follow-up
• With the employer/mentor, identify or apply one workplace example linked to targeted ksb gap learning and corrective practical.
• Retain a suitable record and explain its effect on safety, quality, efficiency or the customer.
workplaceFollowUp.checks:
Trainer preparation
• Check the work area, current technical information, tools/equipment and relevant PPE/RPE.
• Prepare session materials and evidence records: Mood, Motivation and Energy record or programme record.; Individual gap plan; relevant tools/vehicles; technical data; evidence checklist..
• Confirm support needs, reasonable adjustments, any approved recognition-of-prior-learning change and the evidence location. Keep formal assessment, gateway decisions and administration separate from eligible learning.

other.activity: Post-lesson impact: What can apprentices now identify, explain, demonstrate or complete that they could not do at the start? | Follow-up: Who needs additional support, practice or stretch; what is the next action and when will it be reviewed?

howLearningChecked: Start: Record a baseline response on the principles, sequence, risks or controls for targeted ksb gap learning and corrective practical.
During: Use observation, targeted questioning and task checkpoints; correct misconceptions and errors before progression.
End: Review the completed evidence, require correction after feedback and use an exit explanation linked to workplace application.
assessment.impactMeasure:
• Compare the recorded starting-point response with the completed end task and corrected evidence.
• Record one outcome: Not yet secure / Developing / Secure / Exceeding.
• Use the outcome to set targeted support, further practice, progression or stretch.
